# Tobit Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_004_page_001.jpg

---

**4:1** On that day Tobit remembered the money he had deposited with Gabael in Rages of Media,

**4:2** and he said to himself, "I have prayed for death — so why have I not called my son Tobias and told him about this money before I die?"

**4:3** He called him and said: "My son, when I die, give me a proper burial, and do not dishonor your mother. Honor her all the days of your life; do what pleases her, and do not cause her grief.

**4:4** Remember, my son, that she faced many dangers for your sake when she carried you in the womb. When she dies, bury her beside me in the same tomb.

**4:5** All your days, my son, keep the Lord our God in mind, and refuse to sin or transgress his commandments. Practice righteousness all the days of your life, and do not walk in the paths of wrongdoing.

**4:6** For if you act in truth, your deeds will prosper — as they do for all who practice righteousness.

**4:7** Give alms [eleēmosynē] from your possessions, and do not let your eye be grudging when you give. Do not turn your face away from any poor person, and God will not turn his face away from you.

**4:8** Give alms in proportion to what you have. If you have much, give more; if you have little, do not be afraid to give according to that little.

**4:9** In so doing you are storing up a good treasure for yourself against a day of necessity.

**4:10** For almsgiving delivers from death and keeps a man from going down into the darkness.

**4:11** Almsgiving is a great offering before the Most High, a great confidence, for all who practice it.

**4:12** Beware of all fornication, my son. First of all, take a wife from the descendants of your fathers — do not take a foreign wife, one who is not of your father's tribe. For we are sons of the prophets. Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — our fathers of old — remember, my son, that every one of them took wives from among their own kindred, and they were blessed in their children, and their descendants will inherit the land.

**4:13** And now, my son, love your kindred, and do not let your heart be proud toward the sons and daughters of your people when you take a wife from among them. For pride leads to ruin and great disorder, and laziness leads to poverty and want — idleness is the mother of famine.

**4:14** Do not let the wages of any man who works for you remain with you overnight; pay him at once. And if you serve God faithfully, you will be recompensed. Be careful, my son, in all your deeds, and be well-disciplined in all your conduct.

**4:15** What you hate, do not do to anyone. Do not drink wine to excess, and do not let drunkenness be your traveling companion.

**4:16** Share your bread with the hungry, and give your garments to the naked. From all your abundance, give alms — and do not let your eye be stingy in giving.

**4:17** Lay your bread on the graves of the righteous, but do not give to sinners.

**4:18** Seek counsel from every wise person, and do not despise any useful advice.

**4:19** At all times bless the Lord your God, and ask him to direct your paths and make your plans succeed. For no nation possesses wisdom of itself — the Lord himself gives every good thing. He humbles whomever he wills, just as he wills. And now, my son, keep these commandments in your heart; do not let them fade.

**4:20** Now let me tell you about the ten talents of silver I deposited with Gabael son of Gabrias at Rages in Media.

**4:21** Do not be afraid, my son, because we have become poor. You have great wealth if you fear God, flee from every sin, and do what is good in the sight of the Lord your God.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on the core structure of Tobit's testament. The negative Golden Rule at v. 15 was preserved by all in essentially the same form: "What you hate, do not do to anyone." The patriarchal list in v. 12 (Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob) was retained in full by all translators. The poverty-is-not-real-poverty theme of v. 21 was unanimously treated as the chapter's theological capstone.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA's Resolution |
|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| 4:7 | "do eleēmosynē" (untranslated) | "give alms" | "give generously to those in need" | "give alms [eleēmosynē]" — LOGOS's "alms" with EMET's transliteration in brackets for scholarly reference |
| 4:8 | "do-not be-afraid to-give eleēmosynē" | "do not be afraid to give according to that little" | "don't be afraid to give from even that" | LOGOS — full clause retained; PNEUMA's "even that" too colloquial |
| 4:10 | "does-not allow [a-man] to-enter into-the darkness" | "prevents a man from going down into the darkness" | "keeps people out of the darkness" | LOGOS — "going down into the darkness" preserves the Sheol imagery |
| 4:11 | "A-great confidence before the-Most-High is eleēmosynē" | "a great offering of confidence before the Most High" | "no greater offering before God Most High" | Blend: "a great offering before the Most High, a great confidence" — preserves both *megalē pistis* and *parastasis* |
| 4:13 | "in-arrogance there-is ruin and great disorder" | "in pride there is ruin and great instability" | "pride leads to disaster and chaos" | LOGOS — "disorder" (EMET) and "chaos" (PNEUMA) both work; "instability" (LOGOS) most precise for *akatastasia* |
| 4:15 | "Wine to-excess do-not drink" | "Do not drink wine to excess" | "Don't drink too much wine" | LOGOS — natural order without PNEUMA's colloquialism |
| 4:17 | "Pour out your-bread upon the-grave of-the righteous" | "Spread your bread on the grave" | "Lay bread at the graves of the righteous" | PNEUMA's "lay" is natural; combined with LOGOS's "graves of the righteous" — "Lay your bread on the graves of the righteous" |
| 4:19 | "not every nation has-counsel" | "no nation possesses wisdom of itself" | "no nation figures things out on its own" | LOGOS — theologically precise; PNEUMA too casual for this solemn prayer |
| 4:20 | "I-make-known to-you the-ten-talents of-silver" | "Let me tell you now about the ten talents" | "there's something practical I need to tell you" | LOGOS — direct and clear; PNEUMA loses the monetary specificity |
| 4:21 | "you-have many things if you-fear God" | "You have great wealth if you fear God" | "You are rich in what matters" | LOGOS — "great wealth" balances the literal (EMET) and dynamic (PNEUMA) well |
